title: M/S Shree Gopala Iron (India) Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. And Others
coram: Krishna Murari, J. & Mrs. Vijay Lakshmi, J.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed for want of prosecution; interim order vacated
headnote: An industrial consumer challenged a U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. bill applying the New Tariff for 2012-13 from 1 October 2012, though the tariff was published in the newspaper on 23 October 2012. It did not dispute the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission's determination; it said Regulation 139(2) of the UPERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2004, section 24(7) of the U.P. Electricity Reforms Act, 1999 and Clause 3.8(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 allow a tariff to take effect only seven days after publication, so the New Tariff could operate from 31 October 2012 and not from 1 October 2012. On 27 November 2012 the Division Bench held that the matter required consideration, issued notice, and directed that supply would not be disconnected on the impugned bill if, from 1 November 2012, bills were paid at the New Tariff, October 2012 was paid at the prior tariff, pre-October amounts in that bill were paid, and a bank guarantee covered the October difference, all without prejudice. On 25 April 2014 none appeared for the petitioner in the revised call. The writ was dismissed and the interim order vacated. The Court did not decide whether the New Tariff could be given retrospective effect.
facts:
M/S Shree Gopala Iron (India) Pvt. Ltd. challenged a U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. electricity bill applying the New Tariff for 2012-13 from 1 October 2012. Counsel said UPPCL published that tariff in the newspaper on 23 October 2012 yet made it effective from 1 October 2012. The petitioner did not dispute the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission's determination; it objected only to retrospective operation. Invoking Regulation 139(2) of the UPERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2004, section 24(7) of the U.P. Electricity Reforms Act, 1999, Clause 3.8(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and section 62(6) of the Electricity Act, 2003, it argued that a published tariff takes effect only seven days after publication, so the New Tariff could operate from 31 October 2012, not from 1 October 2012.

On 27 November 2012 notice issued and disconnection was stayed on payment and bank-guarantee conditions. On 25 April 2014 none appeared in the revised call.

holding_units.clause: 3.8(a) (tariff takes effect seven days after publication)
holding_units.topic: Challenge to retrospective New Tariff; writ dismissed for want of prosecution
holding_units.holding: On 27 November 2012 the Court recorded the petitioner's case that the New Tariff for 2012-13, published on 23 October 2012, could not be given effect from 1 October 2012 because Clause 3.8(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, section 24(7) of the U.P. Electricity Reforms Act, 1999 and Regulation 139(2) of the 2004 Conduct of Business Regulations provide that a tariff takes effect only seven days after publication, and because section 62(6) of the Electricity Act, 2003 bars recovery in excess of the determined tariff. It held that the matter required consideration, issued notice, and, pending admission, directed that supply would not be disconnected on the impugned bill if (i) from 1 November 2012 the petitioner paid at the New Tariff, (ii) October 2012 was paid at the prior tariff by 10 December 2012, (iii) any pre-October amount in that bill was paid by that date, and (iv) a bank guarantee for the October difference was furnished by that date, failing which the interim would stand vacated, all without prejudice, with surcharge and interest recoverable if the writ failed. On 25 April 2014 none appeared for the petitioner even in the revised call; the writ was dismissed and the interim order vacated, without construing Clause 3.8 or deciding retrospective effect.
holding_units.qualifier: Interlocutory 27.11.2012; dismissed for non-appearance on 25.4.2014 without a merits construction.

principle_tags.application: After a 27.11.2012 without-prejudice stay of disconnection on a bill applying the New Tariff from 1.10.2012, none appeared for the petitioner in the revised call of 25.4.2014; the writ was dismissed and the interim order vacated, leaving the Clause 3.8 / retrospective-tariff point undecided.
The case was called in the revised list; no one appeared to press the writ, which was accordingly dismissed.

not_decided.point: Whether the New Tariff for 2012-13, published on 23.10.2012, could lawfully be given effect from 1.10.2012
not_decided.note: The 27.11.2012 order said only that the matter required consideration and granted a conditional stay; dismissal for non-appearance left retrospective effect unadjudicated.
